title: Preserve completed router turns when checkpoint events are ignored
description:
## Problem

The real Codex run for kbs-894b0c completed valid Python and Rust changes, but its router failed after the agent session while staging the checkpoint event. The exact error was: project/events is ignored and the checkpoint staging path did not force-add it. The branch and draft PR had to be preserved manually.

## Required behavior

Every router checkpoint and agent-turn event must be force-added through the same safe, scoped Git path used for shared router events. A completed or paused agent turn must publish its transcript metadata, checkpoint, branch, draft PR, summary/comment, and configured Review or Blocked state even when project/events is ignored. Nothing may be silently discarded.

## Acceptance criteria

- Python and Rust force-add only the configured event/checkpoint artifact, never unrelated ignored files.
- A completed agent result with an ignored project/events directory creates or updates its draft PR, adds the summary to the issue, and moves the issue to Review.
- A publication failure after a session exists produces a visible issue diagnostic and Review, preserving branch/session/log references.
- Tests exercise the ignored-event failure shape that occurred in kbs-894b0c.
- Git-only coordination remains sufficient; no MQTT, AWS, or automatic closure.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Agent completion preserved in draft PR #307: added a reviewable post-session publication-failure diagnostic and regression coverage for the ignored project/events failure shape. The router then rejected the Codex adapter output with the exact error: Codex router adapter returned invalid result. The raw agent result, branch, and draft PR are preserved; this issue is in Review, not closed. Agent test note: compileall and diff check passed; it reported that its broader Python/Rust environments were unavailable.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Review found the preserved patch incomplete: it does not implement the required force-add checkpoint path in both runtimes. Re-queueing this same issue for another router turn; preserve the existing session, branch, transcript, and draft PR, and continue rather than discarding prior work.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Recovered revision 2 is preserved in draft PR #318. It includes the publication-failure recovery path plus scoped force-add of exact router event artifacts. Local verification: 81 focused Python tests, Rust formatting, and the Rust lifecycle transition test. No issue was closed.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Review rejected draft PR #318: it adds post-session publication recovery only in Python. Rust production `run_issue_router_once` still returns the publication error, releases the claim, and does not preserve the completed turn in Review. Keep #318 and its branch as evidence; continue this issue with equivalent Rust recovery behavior and cross-runtime regression coverage before requesting review again.

comments.author: home
comments.text: New live reproduction: KBS-d9c9ee produced a valid completed Codex result and committed its required Kanbus state with `kbs commit`, but the router wrote `router.conversation` and released all leases without publishing `router.result`, the Review transition, or the agent summary. Recovery required a visible manual Review/comment. The durable record is event `68fb6a5a-b78c-4df6-a8be-adce50b0b06e`, session `01a0bbfe-06c8-7f40-854d-17404253271b`. Extend this recovery work so a valid turn survives this normal agent workflow automatically in both runtimes.
